1.explanation: All of the center-to-center connection snapping logic lives in BpmnConnectSnapping.js, which is registered on the connect.hover, connect.move and connect.end events. In the SequenceFlow branch it only ever snaps the source to mid(source), but never snaps the target to mid(target). Instead it falls back on the generic snapInsideTarget utility (which clamps to the inner padding box) and so never reaches the true center. To restore the expected happy-path behavior you must adjust BpmnConnectSnapping.js to also call setSnapped on the target position (e.g. snapToPosition(event, mid(target))) when creating SequenceFlows.
1.bug_scenario: The user is trying to draw a Sequence Flow directly from the exact center of one Task to the exact center of another Task, but after the introduction of connection previews and grid snapping the end‐points no longer align on the two centers. In the “before” GIF you see the connector snapping neatly center-to-center, whereas in the “after” GIF the connector snaps to an offset position (inside the target’s padding region) and never hits the geometric center of the target.
